measuredFrom.note: CI runs of the coverage branch, whose product code is main's at f33af83f. Each floor is the lowest of the two runs' figures rounded down to one decimal. Weir.Infrastructure and Weir.Api differed between the runs (seven timing-dependent files, mostly background services and watchers), so their four floors are a further 0.1 lower; every other figure was identical in both runs. The four out-of-process floors are from CI run 39124799698 (the contract suite and the E2E smoke, one sample), rounded down to one decimal and a further 0.1 lower because the figure depends on the timing of background services in the server process. The server-core floors were raised in #1060: CI run 39208578019 on main measured 93.0% lines and 84.6% branches for Weir.Core, the new Weir.Core tests add at least 2.8 points of lines and 4.7 of branches (their coverage laid over that run's merged report), and the floors are the sum less 0.1. The server-infrastructure floors were raised in #1060 step 2: CI run 39208578019 on main measured 91.1% lines and 77.9% branches for Weir.Infrastructure; the new Weir.Infrastructure.Tests add 1.7 points of lines and 2.7 of branches on their own (a local run of that one project: 82.4% to 84.1% lines, 71.0% to 73.6% branches), the new tests mostly cover files no Api or Core test runs, and each floor is the CI figure plus 60% of that gain, less 0.1 and rounded down to leave room for the timing-dependent background services. They were raised again in #1060 step 3: the new Weir.Infrastructure.Tests add 1.7 points of lines and 2.4 of branches on their own (a local run of that one project: 84.2% to 86.0% lines, 73.8% to 76.2% branches) and 0.4 of each over the Weir.Api.Tests run (a local merge of the two projects, 92.1% to 92.4% lines, 80.2% to 80.6% branches), so each floor is the previous floor plus 60% of that merged gain, less 0.1 and rounded down.
